title: BESSELY truncates order into 0..=10,000,000 and applies a phase-shifted 2^27-1 limit that admits BESSELY(134217728, 1)
statement: In Excel 16.0.20527.20088, BESSELY(x, n) requires x > 0 and truncates n to an integer in 0..=10,000,000 (#NUM! for n < 0 such as -0.5 or n >= 10,000,001). For large x, Excel checks |x| - phase <= 2^27 - 1 using phase = 0.785398164 for Y0 and 2.356194491 for Y1 (forward recurrence orders require both seeds). Consequently, BESSELY(134217728, 1) is admitted and returns 1.1173873549496432e-05 (0x3ed7ff19f84f233c) because 134,217,728 - 2.356194491 <= 134,217,727, whereas BESSELJ(134217728, 0) returns #NUM! because 134,217,728 - 0.785398164 > 134,217,727. Subnormal operands and intermediates flush to zero.
basis: Measured across all 84 BESSELY readings in DnaCalc dc96l3_bessel and 124 in dcj9k_r25_bessel (Excel 16.0.20527.20088); 2,901/2,905 full-bank BESSELY rows match.
